Owner-stated: turns weren't perfectly on the 5s mark ('pretty close', he pointed at each speaker as he judged the mark) — treat turn BOUNDARIES as approximate (+/- 1-2s slop), not exact, unlike the family_real fixture's precisely self-timed turns. baseline_measured_2026-08-21.cap_raised_2026-08-21_followup: Three parallel experiments run 2026-08-21 raised MAX_SPEAKERS_LOCAL to 6 project-wide (see server/diarize_local.py). On THIS specific file, k=5/6 are now evaluated for the first time — both have low pooled cosine (0.202, 0.284; well under the 0.45 accept threshold), confirming the underlying voices ARE genuinely distinguishable — but both are rejected by the separate MIN_CLUSTER_SECONDS_STRONG duration-evidence floor, so cross_check_num_speakers stays at 4 on this file regardless of the cap. Lowering the duration floor was investigated and found unsafe (breaks 3 pinned calibration tests) and wouldn't even help here (the admitted extra cluster would be a spurious fragment of an already-correctly-identified speaker, not a genuinely recovered one). The real bottleneck for this file is upstream transcript segmentation (welded turns), a separate follow-up not yet started. MAX_SPEAKERS_LOCAL=4 is therefore no longer this fixture's limiter.

scoring_note: This fixture is NOT yet a pinned 100%-accuracy regression test like the synthetic fixtures or test_recording_family_real.wav — the honest current state is a KNOWN, MEASURED SHORTFALL (4 of 6 real speakers found). It exists to track improvement attempts against a fixed real baseline. Score any change by best-permutation accuracy against `approx_turns` (majority time-overlap per pipeline-produced turn, tolerant of the approximate boundaries), AND report num_speakers_detected honestly even if accuracy-scoring is not yet meaningful at the current 4-cluster ceiling.
